Runs the system tx and commits the state into the block. For history and beacon-roots addresses it accepts reverts and halts (unchecked). It also adds failure checks for request contracts.
Runs and finalizes the system call with SYSTEM_ADDRESS, without committing state.

Runs the EIP-2935 system call (environment set up inside transact_blockhashes_contract_call) and commits its state to the database. This is the spec's process-then-incorporate flow, but for one hard-coded target only.
Runs the EIP-4788 beacon-root system call and commits the resulting state. Same pattern as the spec's unchecked system call, limited to one target.
General journal cleanup after a transaction: returns the state and clears logs, transient storage and the journal. Nothing specific to system calls.
Builds the starting gas tracker for any transaction. Not specific to system transactions.
Just passes through to the journal's finalize. General transaction machinery.
Shared execution loop that runs the call frames for any transaction. It doesn't set up a system environment or merge state into the block.
Implements the spec's execute_block (pre-changes, txs, post-changes), which state_transition only calls. It does not apply the diff to state or append to the chain.
Executor constructor that only initializes fields.
Post-block rewards, withdrawals and DAO drain. Part of block execution, not state_transition.
Pre-execution system calls, part of block execution.
Test helper that builds a synthetic block, executes it and compares hooked and unhooked output.
Only builds the EVM/block environment from the header (spec id, blob params). This is execution setup. It does not execute the block, apply state changes or append the block to the chain.

Packs block fields (parent hash, beacon root, ommers, withdrawals) into an execution context for the executor. It reads only from the block, not the chain, and does not execute, apply state or update the chain.

Implements the CALL opcode (and other call kinds): pops the stack, rejects a value transfer in a static context, prices memory, computes access/delegation/value/new-account state gas and the child gas, then dispatches the new call frame with the reservoir and the new-account-charged flag.
Gas portion of call: value-transfer cost, delegated account load and access cost, new-account state gas (EIP-8037), 63/64 child gas and its charge, call stipend.
Pops the memory operands and expands/charges memory for the input and output ranges, i.e. the spec's calculate_gas_extend_memory step for call.
Builds the top-level transaction frame, not the CALL opcode.
Corresponds to the spec's generic_call (depth check, checkpoint, value transfer, precompile, frame setup), which call only invokes.
Unit test for the system call.
Implements to_address_masked, a separate helper CALL only uses.
Call-specific memory growth and charge for the input/output ranges (the extend_memory part of call).
Thin wrapper around load_account_delegated that passes remaining gas; carries CALL's account/delegation access gas logic.
Covers CALL's state-dependent gas: cold access, EIP-7702 delegation cost and code load, new-account cost and EIP-8037 new-account state gas.
General memory resize helper, not CALL logic.
Value transfer between accounts; the spec does this in generic_call/process_message, not in call.
General memory expansion gas helper.
Stipend constant getter; belongs to calculate_message_call_gas.
Computes the 63/64 limit on child gas; belongs to calculate_message_call_gas/max_message_call_gas.
Returns the gas constant for a value transfer.

Full CREATE opcode: static check, pops endowment/offset/size, init-code size limit and cost, memory expansion, base create gas, address from sender nonce, child frame dispatch (generic_create part). Shared with CREATE2 through a const generic.
Only works out the contract address. That matches the separate spec helper compute_contract_address, not create's own logic.
Trivial getter for the init code.
Struct constructor for CreateInputs. No opcode logic.
Cached keccak of the init code, used for CREATE2 addresses. Not part of CREATE.
Setter that replaces the init code and resets the caches.
A generic memory-resize wrapper that every opcode touching memory uses. It matches calculate_gas_extend_memory, which is a separate spec function, and it does nothing specific to CREATE.

Mostly does the job of generic_create: depth check, balance check, nonce bump, checkpoint and frame setup. It also computes the created address from the caller's old nonce, which the spec does inside create (compute_contract_address). So part of create's logic lives here.
Only a config getter for the max initcode size constant. It does not do the size check itself.
A generic memory-expansion helper that charges gas, shared by many opcodes. It corresponds to calculate_gas_extend_memory, not to create.
Equivalent to the spec helper init_code_cost, which create calls. Being a callee does not make it create.
Only a constant lookup for the CREATE base gas. It does no charging or create logic.

Generic call<KIND> instruction. For DELEGATECALL it checks the Homestead fork and pops gas and address. Through its helpers it pops the memory arguments, extends memory, charges access and delegation gas and withholds child gas. It keeps the current target, caller and apparent value, does not transfer value, passes the reservoir and starts the child frame. That is the whole job of the spec delegatecall.

Charges the dynamic access and delegation gas (and state gas). It then works out and charges the 63/64-capped child gas limit. This matches the spec's gas checks plus calculate_message_call_gas and charge_gas, only one part of delegatecall.

Loads the target account, adds the cold-access cost and follows an EIP-7702 delegation, adding its access cost. Returns the code and code hash. This matches the spec's access-cost, calculate_delegation_cost and get_code steps, a sub-part of delegatecall.
Pops the memory input and output offsets and sizes and resizes memory, charging the expansion gas. This is the spec's stack-pop and memory-extension part of delegatecall.
Only checks whether a CallScheme is DelegateCall. Does no delegatecall work.
Test that builds bytecode using DELEGATECALL. It is not an implementation.
Builds the static per-opcode gas table for every opcode, including DELEGATECALL's warm base cost. It is a table of constants, not delegatecall logic.
Precompile input helper that checks whether target equals bytecode address. Not the delegatecall instruction.
Simple getter for the target address.
Turns a stack word into an address. This is the separate spec helper to_address_masked, not delegatecall's logic.
Simple getter for the caller address.
Grows memory over the call's input and output ranges and charges for it. This is delegatecall's memory-extension step.
Simple getter for the call value.
Loads the target account with cold/warm access and EIP-7702 delegation handling, giving the gas, code and hash. This is delegatecall's state-access and delegation-cost step.
Sets up the child frame (depth check, checkpoint, value transfer, precompiles). This is the separate spec function generic_call, which delegatecall only calls.
Simple getter for the gas reservoir.
General-purpose wrapper for growing memory.
General journal function for loading an account.
Utility that counts 32-byte memory words.
General memory resize helper.
General memory resize and gas charge.
Context wrapper around loading an account.
General formula for memory gas cost.
The 63/64 rule for child-call gas. This belongs to calculate_message_call_gas, a separate spec helper.

Covers the first half of generic_create. It reads init code from memory, runs the preflight checks (balance, nonce overflow, depth) that push 0 and clear return data, and warms the destination. It charges the new-account state gas when the destination is not alive, keeps back 1/64 of the gas and passes the reservoir to the child. It also includes the opcode's own pricing, which the spec does elsewhere. The collision check, nonce bump, child frame and outcome resolution happen in other functions.

Sets up the child create frame: bumps the caller nonce, computes the created address, warms it, runs the collision check through create_account_checkpoint and builds the child interpreter with the gas limit and reservoir. This is the collision and dispatch part of generic_create. It also repeats the depth and balance checks.

Handles the outcome step for CREATE. It sets return data to the child's output on revert and clears it otherwise. It merges the child's gas back into the parent, pushes the created address or 0, and refunds the new-account state gas when a charged create failed. Its CALL branch is separate logic.

Runs the collision check (code or nonce present means CreateCollision), which matches account_deployable in generic_create. It also marks the account created, sets its nonce to 1 and moves the value, which the spec does inside process_create. This is a sub-piece of the lifecycle.

Decides whether the create state-gas charge is refunded: the create failed or produced no address, and the charge was taken. This is the condition for credit_state_gas_refund in generic_create's outcome step. The actual refund is applied in return_result.

General frame plumbing. It forwards the NewFrame action and, once the frame returns, commits or reverts the checkpoint through return_create and wraps the outcome along with the charged-state-gas flag. That is the job of process_create/process_message, not generic_create.
Builds the top-level frame input for a transaction, including the state-gas charge for a create transaction. This is transaction-level work, not the CREATE opcode's child-frame lifecycle.

Merges a finished child frame's gas into the parent (rollback, spend_all on halt, adds state gas spent, refunds, returns the reservoir). It works for calls and creates alike and matches the spec's separate incorporate_child callee. It has none of generic_create's own logic: preflight checks, new-account charge, collision check, gas withholding, nonce increment, child dispatch, or giving back the NEW_ACCOUNT charge on failure.
The REVERT opcode itself. It rejects the opcode before Byzantium, then calls return_inner with Revert, which pops offset and size, expands memory, sets the output and ends the frame.
Shared helper for RETURN and REVERT. It pops offset and size, charges for memory growth, reads the output from memory and sets the return action. The Revert outcome is passed in by the caller.
Builds a revert result for a precompile, not the opcode.
Converts the halt reason in an execution result.
Turns a precompile's status into an interpreter result.
Only checks whether a result is a revert.
Generic: records the next interpreter action and stops the loop. Any halting opcode uses it.
Low-level resize of the memory buffer. A shared helper, not REVERT logic.
Builds a Return action from a result, output and gas. Generic plumbing.
Subtracts gas from what remains. Matches the spec's charge_gas, not revert.
Wrapper around the shared memory-expansion helper, which matches calculate_gas_extend_memory plus charge_gas.
Slice read from memory. A generic memory_read_bytes-style helper.
Passes through to the gas tracker's charge. Matches charge_gas.
Memory-gas bookkeeping helper.
Handles a finished frame (commit or revert the journal). That is the caller's side (process_message), not the opcode.
Converts a byte length to a word count.
Generic memory expansion with gas. Matches calculate_gas_extend_memory and charge_gas, which every memory opcode uses.
Slow path of the generic memory expansion: charges gas and resizes.
Rolls back journaled state. That happens in message processing after the Revert is raised, not in the opcode.
Finishes a CREATE frame (code deposit, commit or revert). Not REVERT.
Memory cost formula. Matches calculate_memory_gas_cost.

Includes the delegation logic (detect 7702 target, add warm read plus extra cold cost if the target is cold) inside a larger call-cost function that also charges for the account's own cold access and new-account cost.
Finds the delegation designation and loads the target to record whether it is cold. The caller computes the gas; this function does not.
Host default version of the same thing: finds the 7702 target and reports whether it is cold, without computing a cost.
Applies authorizations and charges for writing them (set_delegation's job), not for accessing a delegation target.
Runs authorization-list processing and returns the refund. Not about delegation access cost.
Gas parameter getter for access-list addresses.
Gas parameter getter for access-list storage keys.
Checks the sender's code and nonce before execution.
Applies the authorization list. Only calls bytecode.is_eip7702() for the delegation check and has no length or marker logic of its own.
Checks a txpool validation outcome enum variant. Has nothing to do with delegation code.
Checks that a BLS12-381 field element is below the modulus.
Looks up a legacy JUMPDEST in the jump table.
EIP-3607 sender code check and nonce check. Calls is_eip7702() rather than implementing the delegation check.
Processes the auth list and only calls bytecode.is_eip7702(). The length and 0xef0100 prefix check is not done here, so it is a caller, not an implementation.

Resolves the 7702 designation and charges warm plus the cold extra for the delegated account, warming it and returning its code. Also charges target access and new-account costs, so the spec logic sits inside a larger function.
Thin wrapper that only calls load_account_delegated with the remaining gas.
Finds the delegated address and loads (warms) it, recording whether it was cold. Charges no gas.
Host default: detects the delegation, warms the delegate and reports whether it was cold. Charges no gas.
Applies authorizations (sets delegation designations and charges state gas); does not resolve a call target's delegation.
For a top-level call it resolves the recipient's delegation inline, charges warm then the cold difference, warms the account and loads its code. This is embedded in tx frame creation.

Call-setup helper. The delegation check, warm/cold cost choice and warming happen in load_account_delegated_handle_error. This function deducts the returned dynamic gas (which presumably includes the delegated-address access cost) along with transfer, state gas and the 63/64 forwarding rule. It covers the charging part of the spec function, mixed in with other call costs.
Does the spec's condition: when the account is empty and value is sent, it works out new_account_state_gas under EIP-8037. It only returns the amount; the caller deducts it.
Takes the state gas worked out by load_account_delegated and deducts it with state_gas!. This is the charge half of the spec logic for CALL-family opcodes, inside the wider CALL gas calculation.
At the transaction level, it charges new_account_state_gas when tx value is non-zero and the recipient is empty. This is the spec check written inline inside frame setup.
In SELFDESTRUCT, it charges new_account_state_gas when value goes to a target that does not exist (had_value && !target_exists). This is the same check written inline in the opcode.
Only reads the value from the CallValue enum. It charges nothing.
Works out the EIP-2780 intrinsic regular gas (base, cold access, value cost). It has no check for whether the account is alive and no state gas.
Getter that returns the target address.
Returns the older regular-gas new-account cost from EIP-161. It is not the EIP-8037 state gas charge.

Covers the front half of process_call: the depth-limit check, the journal checkpoint (the snapshot), the value transfer and running precompiles, with commit or revert for precompiles. Running the bytecode and rolling back state on error happen elsewhere.
Covers the back half of process_call: when a call frame finishes, it commits the checkpoint on success or reverts it on error (the spec's restore_tx_state on error).
This is the opcode loop: it steps through instructions until something halts it, then records the halt. That matches the spec's while-loop and its handling of exceptional halts.

Runs in the parent frame after a child returns. It pushes the success flag, copies the return data and merges the child's gas into the parent, which is the call opcode's job. It also refunds the upfront state-gas charge, which is the opposite of a charge.
Sets up a CREATE frame (nonce bump, address derivation, account creation). That matches process_create_message, not process_call.
Only formats error enum values as display strings.
Covers the precompile branch of process_call: it looks up and runs the precompile at the code address and turns the output into an interpreter result.
Covers the opcode-loop branch: it runs the interpreter over the frame's code and handles the action that comes back.
Implements restore_state_gas, a separate spec function that process_call only calls.
Wrapper that passes straight through to JournalInner.transfer_loaded, which does process_call's value-transfer and transfer-log step.
Implements forfeit_remaining_gas, a separate helper that process_call only calls.
Wrapper for copy_tx_state (taking the snapshot), a separate helper.
Wrapper for restore_tx_state, a separate helper.
Does process_call's value-transfer step: moves the ether and emits the EIP-7708 transfer log, skipping the log when sender and recipient are the same.
Does process_call's error-path gas handling: rolls back state gas on revert or halt, uses up all remaining gas on halt, then hands what is left back to the parent.
Implements the snapshot (copy_tx_state equivalent), a separate helper.
Implements restore_tx_state, a separate helper.
Implements emit_transfer_log, a separate helper.

SLOAD opcode handler: pops the key, loads storage for the target address and charges the extra cold cost when the slot is cold. The journal marks the slot accessed. Assumes the base warm cost of 100 is charged by revm's static gas table, which was not in the code shown.
Journal-level read: loads the slot, marks it accessed or warm and returns the present value. Covers the access-set update and get_storage, but has no gas or stack handling.
Thin wrapper around the journal storage read with warm or cold tracking. Covers the state lookup only, not gas or the stack.
Default trait method that delegates to sload_skip_cold_load(false). Storage read plus access marking only.
Host storage read that delegates to sload_skip_cold_load and is used by the pre-Berlin opcode path. Storage lookup only.
Journal impl that calls inner.sload_assume_account_present to read the slot and track whether it is cold. State part only.
Sets SLOAD's static base cost to WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST (100) from Berlin on. That is the warm-access part of sload's gas charge.
Generic instruction-pointer move used by every opcode. Nothing specific to sload.

Core storage-slot load. Decides whether the slot is cold (not yet loaded this transaction and not in the access list), marks it warm, journals it as warmed and reads the value from the DB. Covers the accessed_storage_keys check/add and get_storage.
Generic gas deduction with an out-of-gas flag. Not specific to sload.
Generic interpreter dispatch loop: charges static gas and runs the opcode.
Thin wrapper that only passes the call to JournalInner.sload_assume_account_present.
Host wrapper that passes the call to the journal and maps errors. No sload logic of its own.
Config getter for the cold storage cost parameter. It does no charging.
Gets the account, loads the slot through sload_concrete_error and returns its present value with the cold flag. This is the storage-read part of sload.

This is the warm/cold test from sload's gas step, matching the spec's accessed_storage_keys check. revm keeps a cold flag and transaction id on each slot instead of an access set. It doesn't mark the key warm, charge gas, read storage or push the value, and sstore likely uses it too.

The TLOAD opcode handler. It checks for Cancun, takes the key from the stack top, reads transient storage for the current target and writes the value back in place. The fixed gas cost is presumably charged through the instruction table.
Only reads the transient storage value, which is the counterpart of get_transient_storage, a function the spec's tload calls. It doesn't do the opcode's stack or gas work.
A wrapper that passes the call down to the internal transient storage read. It doesn't implement the opcode.
A host-level wrapper that passes the call to the journal's tload. It is only the storage lookup the opcode uses.
A journal wrapper that passes the call to the inner transient storage read. It is a callee, not the opcode.
Implements the transient storage lookup (get_transient_storage) that is the core operation of TLOAD; no stack/gas/pc handling.
Generic instruction pointer advance helper, not TLOAD-specific.
Generic gas deduction primitive (charge_gas analogue); no TLOAD logic.
Generic interpreter dispatch loop; applies static gas/pc for all opcodes and calls the instruction.
Defines TLOAD static gas of 100, the charge_gas(OPCODE_TLOAD) part of tload split out into revm's static gas table.

Subtracts the intrinsic cost, caps execution gas at the 7825 tx gas limit cap minus intrinsic execution gas, and puts the overflow in StateReservoir. Same split as the spec, except it also pre-subtracts intrinsic state gas.
Allocates EVM stack memory and has nothing to do with gas.
Stack pool allocation, not a gas split.
Receives gasAvailable already allocated and uses it for delegations and execution. It does not split the gas itself.
Implements the GAS opcode.
Computes only the state-reservoir part, as max(0, gasLimit - intrinsicState - cap). It does not compute the execution-gas grant.
Computes the transaction's blob gas times the fee per blob gas from the header's excess blob gas, with an overflow check. Same as total_blob_gas * blob_gas_price.
Same logic as [0]: blob gas times the fee per blob gas. It also returns the fee per blob gas as an extra output.
Interface declaration only. It has no body and no logic.
Multiplies by the transaction's maxFeePerBlobGas, not the blob gas price derived from excess blob gas. This is the max-fee check, a different calculation.
Computes only the blob gas price (spec calculate_blob_gas_price), a separate spec function that this one calls. Borderline: could be argued as partial.

Computes memory expansion cost for a single (location, length) range: skips zero length, computes new size, charges only if it grows past current size. Spec iterates a list of extensions; this handles one per call.
Wrapper with inlined fast-path check that the range already fits in memory (spec's after_size <= before_size skip), then delegates to CalculateMemoryCost and charges gas.
Rounds sizes up to words and computes the cost delta between the old and new memory sizes, updating Size (like current_size = after_size). Core piece of the per-extension computation.
Frame transaction intrinsic/floor gas budget calculation; not memory expansion.
Charges the fixed low gas cost for SIGNEXTEND; unrelated to memory.
Implements total_cost - already_paid with the memory cost formula (3*words + words^2/512) over word counts; the arithmetic core of the spec function.

Only checks memory bounds: whether offset+length fits within MaxMemorySize and a u64, then returns the raw end offset. No ceil32 rounding, no memory gas cost and no expansion size, so it does none of the gas calculation the spec function does.
Sums blob counts across a whole block's transactions, then converts the total to gas. The spec's per-tx logic is inlined in a block-level aggregate.
Blob count (hashes length, or 0) times GasPerBlob for one tx, the same as the spec.
Calculates the blob fee by calling CalculateBlobGas(transaction). It is a caller, not the gas calculation.
Interface declaration for the blob-fee calculation only.
Computes the max blob fee and does blobCount*GasPerBlob inline. Borderline: the count is passed in and the function's job is fee validation.
Gives only the blob count part (versioned hashes length, or 0), without multiplying by GasPerBlob.
Checks remaining < cost (fails, OOG) else subtracts cost from gas — matches charge_gas_from_meter.
Same check-and-subtract for a compile-time constant cost; negative remainder signals OOG.
Code-deposit flow that delegates charging to TryConsumeStateAndExecutionGas; a caller, not the meter charge itself.
Empty refund/repay hook for state gas spill; opposite direction.
Resets BAL data meter state; not execution gas charging.
Meters BAL data bytes against a floor limit; not gas_left deduction.
Code deposit and failure handling; calls UpdateGas/TryConsume helpers rather than implementing the charge.
Performs only the subtraction; the out-of-gas check lives in UpdateGas.
Takes from the reservoir first, then takes the spill from gas.Value, clears the reservoir, adds to StateGasSpill and fails on out-of-gas. This matches the spec's charge logic.
Computes only the spill amount (cost minus the positive reservoir), one piece of the spec's charge logic.
Wrapper that charges execution gas and then calls TryConsumeStateGas. It only calls the implementation.
Empty interface default for repaying spill. The opposite direction and has no logic.
Puts refunded state gas back into gas_left and the reservoir. A refund, not a charge.
Refunds state gas into gas_left and the reservoir. The opposite of a charge.
Takes back a previously credited state gas refund. Refund bookkeeping, not the state gas charge.
Empty interface default for taking back a refund.
Generic raw subtraction of gas.Value. It has no state gas reservoir or spill logic.
Generic gas consume with a bounds check. [0] uses it, but it has no state gas logic of its own.

Inside the blob branch, BuyGas works out the blob gas price and rejects the transaction when MaxFeePerBlobGas is below it. That is the spec check, written inline among the gas-buying and balance logic.
For frame transactions with blobs, it works out the blob gas price and rejects a MaxFeePerBlobGas below it. This is the spec check written inline inside the larger frame-transaction execution.
Only formats the error message. It does no checking.
Computes the blob count times gas per blob times the fee cap, the most the sender could pay, for the balance check. It does not compare the cap with the price.
For each blob-carrying transaction in a block, it rejects a MaxFeePerBlobGas below the blob gas price. That check is inline, alongside the block blob-gas total and header checks.
Only works out the blob gas price, the calculate_blob_gas_price helper. No fee-cap comparison.
Works out the per-unit blob gas price and the transaction's total blob fee. No comparison with the cap.
Blob gas price calculation (memoized), which the spec function calls rather than implements.
Blob gas price calculation using the fake exponential.
The fake_exponential math helper.
Does the whole LIFO refund credit. It splits the amount into a part that lowers state-gas used and a pending remainder, and sends both through the gas_left-up-to-spill, then reservoir path.
Does the LIFO split (gas_left up to the unrefunded spill, rest to the reservoir) only for the part capped by refundable state-gas used. It also lowers StateGasUsed.
Does the LIFO split for the pending remainder: gas_left up to the unrefunded spill, then the reservoir.
Only forwards to CreditStateGasRefund and has no logic of its own.
Caller: unwinds a halted child and calls CreditStateGasRefund.
Does the reverse: takes back a credited refund from the reservoir and from usage.
Getter that only reads the remaining unrefunded spill (spill minus refunded). It does no crediting.
Computes from_gas_left = min(amount, spill) and records it as refunded, which matches the spec's spill decrement.
Sets the gas meter's remaining value to 0, which is the spec's forfeit. The spec's spill assertion is only a check and changes no state.
Empty tracer hook that only reports remaining gas.
Abstract setter for any remaining-gas value. It is not the burn on an exceptional halt.
Getter that reads remaining gas.
Empty tracer hook that reports gas per operation.
Empty tracer hook that reports gas per action.
Repays min(reservoir, outstanding spill) from the reservoir to gas left. Raises StateGasSpillRefunded instead of lowering the spill, which gives the same result.
Empty default on the interface; the real logic is in EthereumGasPolicy.
Computes the outstanding spill (spill - refunded) that RepayStateGasSpill uses in its min, i.e. the spec's state_gas_spilled.
Undoes a child create frame's state gas after a code deposit failure; this is not a spill repayment.
Works out how much of a state gas charge spills past the reservoir (charge side, not repayment).

Revert-path rollback: returns the child's net spill to the parent's gas_left and the rest of the child's state gas (reservoir + used - spill) to the parent's reservoir, which is the same as resetting to the baseline. The refund discard seems to come from dropping the child frame's state (not traced).
Halt version of the same rollback: returns only the reservoir-funded part and skips the spill refill because the halt burns gas_left. This is the halt half of the spec function.
Transaction-level halt reset: puts the reservoir back to its starting value, sets used back to the intrinsic floor and zeroes the spill. This is the reset-to-baseline step for the top frame.
Empty default interface method; it does nothing.
Empty default interface method; it does nothing.
Frame-pop orchestration that only calls the refund-removal and restore-on-halt functions.
Helper that computes the net spill, i.e. how much gets refilled into gas_left during the rollback.
Takes back state-gas refunds credited during the failed frame from the reservoir and used counters. This is part of rolling the reservoir back to the baseline.
Removes the frame's advanced state-gas refund when the frame is undone, the equivalent of discarding refunds accrued on the undone changes.
Main settlement: pre-refund gas, capped refund, max(post-refund, floor), EIP-7778 block exec gas and state gas; also pays the refund.
Computes pre-refund gas and the refund capped at a fifth.
Computes the block exec gas (pre-refund minus state, floored) and the block state gas.
Settlement formula for the top-level halt path: limit minus reservoir, capped refund, floor, block gas.
max(gasUsed - stateGas, floor): the execution_gas_used step.
Frame-tx settlement does the same refund cap, floor and block-gas split; also pays fees and finalizes.
Refund cap min(spent/5, refund).
Pre-execution gas limit validation.
Only picks the floor gas value.
Tracer validation for CREATE; not gas.
tx_gas - gas_left - state_gas_left (gas_used_before_refund).
Fail-path settlement: pre-refund gas, floor and block exec/state gas.
Pays the refund and packages amounts already computed elsewhere.
Thin wrapper over the refund-cap computation.

Does the price part: min(maxFee, priority + base). Legacy txs reach this branch because their fee fields are all set to gasPrice. It skips the check that maxFee covers the base fee, which lives elsewhere.
A virtual hook in the transaction processor that hands off to [0]. It is the processor's way of computing the effective price, with no base-fee check.
Does the spec's check: fails when baseFee > fee cap, except for free txs. Also computes the priority fee as min(maxPriority, feeCap - baseFee). Returns the premium, not the full effective price.
Only calls CalculateEffectiveGasPrice to work out the most a tx could cost (gas limit times price, plus value).
Only calls CalculateEffectiveGasPrice to build gas info for receipts and RPC.
Metrics: collects gas price statistics for a block using CalculateEffectiveGasPrice.
A wrapper around [2]: the processor's hook for the base-fee check and the priority fee.

Turns the failed base-fee check (via [6]) into the MaxFeePerGasBelowBaseFee error, matching the spec's InsufficientMaxFeePerGasError. The effective price arrives as an input; most of the function is buying gas.
Inline balanceCheck = GasLimit*MaxFeePerGas (1559) or GasLimit*effectiveGasPrice is the spec computation, embedded in the full buy-gas/balance logic.
Computes maxGas*MaxFeePerGas (the spec's max gas fee) for frame txs, then adds blob cost.
Computes the effective priority fee/tip, not gas_limit*fee cap.
Error message string only.
Selects the fee cap (MaxFeePerGas else GasPrice) as the spec does but doesn't multiply by gas limit.
Computes premium per gas vs base fee, not the max gas fee.
Inlines the spec check for regular txs (tx.Nonce vs state nonce, too high/too low errors), then also increments the nonce.
Builds only the too-low/too-high error. The comparison is done by its caller ValidateFrameTxNonce.
Does the nonce equality check with too-low/too-high errors for frame txs, plus keyed nonces (EIP-8250). Does not cover the regular tx path.
Writes incremented nonces (consumption), does no check.
Builds a footprint record. Its nonce comparison only decides whether to cache the footprint, not tx validity.
Only throws an exception after a transaction fails to execute; no decoding.
Checks block transactions are well formed and the minimum block gas; no type dispatch or RLP decoding.
Decodes inputs for the EIP-2537 BLS precompile in parallel, not transactions.
Decodes a BLS field element, not a transaction.
Removes malformed frame transactions from the transaction pool during block building.
Holds the per-fork list of allowed transaction types, which the spec encodes in the type bytes it accepts. It is a yes/no check that [6] calls, does no decoding, and accepts any unlisted type.
Rejects transaction types the fork does not enable, like the spec's TransactionTypeError branch. No RLP decoding or empty-input check.

Tells you whether a tx type carries an EIP-2930 access list: it accepts AccessList and every later type, and leaves out deposit and frame types. That is the same type check as isinstance against AccessListCapableTransaction.
Interface method that returns an access list for system contracts from a block. It does not check whether a transaction has one.
Prewarms state from system access lists. This is cache warming, not a transaction type check.
Enumerator over the entries of an access list.
Constructor for the access list object.
Builder that creates an access list.
Validates the signature's chain id against the configured chain. It does not compute an EIP-155 signing hash.
Fork config that turns on the EIP-155 flag. It does no hashing.
Validates an EIP-7702 authorization tuple. It has nothing to do with the legacy EIP-155 signing hash.
Builds a JWT auth token. It has nothing to do with transaction hashing.
Loads genesis chain parameters, including the EIP-155 transition block. It does no hashing.
Only turns on the Berlin fork flags (EIP-2565/2929/2930). It computes no hash.
Non-generic enumerator forwarder on AccessList. No signing hash logic.
Empty Dispose on the access-list enumerator.
Resets the enumerator's indices. No RLP encoding or keccak.
Writes the delegation code to the authority account. It does not compute the type-4 transaction signing hash.
Only increments a metrics counter.
Only increments a metrics counter.
Checks whether code is a delegation designator. No hashing of the transaction.
Classifies an account change as a deployment for a diff view. No signing hash.

Runs the whole block body: pre-execution system calls (beacon root, blockhash), the transaction loop, then FinalizeBlock for withdrawals, requests and the BAL. The BAL item-limit check is done elsewhere.
Covers the post-transaction half of apply_body: withdrawals, execution requests and building/setting the block access list. It also handles receipts and roots, which apply_body does not.
Thin wrapper that only forwards to the process_withdrawals equivalent.
Builds the EIP-2935 system call to the history contract with the parent hash, which is one of the pre-execution steps written inline in apply_body.
Interface declaration only.
No-op implementation.
Implements the process_withdrawals callee, not apply_body itself.
Merges, encodes and hashes the BAL, which is the job of build_block_access_list plus header hashing. That is a separate spec function.
Forwards to the beacon-root handler, which corresponds to the process_unchecked_system_transaction callee.
Item-limit predicate belonging to validate_block_access_list_gas_limit, a separate function.
Delegating wrapper for the beacon-root system call.
Delegating wrapper for the blockhash store.
Implements apply_body's loop that runs process_transaction over each transaction in the block.
Wrapper for the process_general_purpose_requests callee.
Wrapper for the process_withdrawals callee.
Accessor for the post-execution processor.
Parallel or sequential transaction loop; same role as apply_body's transaction loop.
Processes a single transaction (process_transaction), not the block-level loop.
Wrapper for the execution-requests callee.
BAL gas-limit check on produced blocks, i.e. validate_block_access_list_gas_limit, a separate function.
Internal helper that merges BAL slices.
Validates a supplied BAL's hash, size and bounds in the block validator. This is not body execution.
Implements the validate_block_access_list_gas_limit callee.

Computes the parent gas target and the equal, above and below target branches, with the minimum +1 when the fee rises, the same as the spec. Adds fork-block and minimum-fee handling. The gas-limit check is done elsewhere.
Only passes the call through to the spec's base fee calculator.
Works out a transaction's effective priority fee from the base fee. It doesn't compute the base fee.
Works out a transaction's premium per gas. It only uses the base fee.
Works out a transaction's effective gas price. It doesn't compute the base fee.
Checks whether the sender has enough balance during block production.
Implements the gas-limit bound check, which matches check_gas_limit, not the base fee calculation.

Runs the admission sequence (static validation, effective gas price, sender recovery, EOA check, balance check, nonce check, gas allocation), then also executes the tx. check_transaction is inlined in this larger function.
Static admission checks: intrinsic and floor gas, EIP-8037 max total gas cap, and the per-tx block gas limit check through ValidateGas. Only part of check_transaction.
Does the max_gas_fee + value balance check, the max fee per gas check and the blob fee checks from check_transaction, but also debits the sender.
The InvalidSenderError 'not EOA' check from check_transaction.
Wrapper around the gas split, which is the separate spec function allocate_evm_gas.
Block-level blob validation, including the header blob_gas_used check. Not transaction admission.
Frame-transaction (EIP-8141) validation prefix simulation.
Computes gas info for receipts and RPC.
Frame-transaction max cost calculation.
Computes the recipient, using the contract address for creations. That is the recipient step done inline in check_transaction.
EIP-8037 2D block gas inclusion check. Matches check_block_gas_capacity, a separate spec function.
Effective gas price helper. Matches calculate_effective_gas_price.
Blob fee calculation helper.
Holds the EIP-3607/7702 logic for the not-EOA sender check that is inline in check_transaction.
Per-tx block gas inclusion check during block processing. Matches check_block_gas_capacity.
Sender recovery. Matches recover_sender.
Warms access-list, coinbase, sender and recipient during execution setup.
Splits gas into the execution grant and the state reservoir. Matches allocate_evm_gas.
Checks the intrinsic minimum gas and that tx.gas fits the block gas limit, part of the admission checks.
Recovers the sender and creates a missing account. Matches recover_sender.
Intrinsic gas calculation.
Effective gas price wrapper.
Does the nonce mismatch check from check_transaction, then increments the nonce, which the spec does elsewhere.
Builds the top-level frame's execution environment and loads code, not the transaction environment.

Processes the EIP-7702 authorization list (recovers authorities, charges state and write gas, bumps nonces or creates accounts, sets delegation code). That is the spec's set_delegation step during execution, not the sender, nonce, balance, fee and block-capacity checks or the tx-environment construction in check_transaction.
Top-level per-block driver: prepares, executes (ProcessBlock), then validates post-state against suggested header; pre-execution size/header/ommers checks live in BlockValidator.ValidateBlock.
Executes the block body (system calls, txs) and finalizes, corresponding to apply_body plus root computation part of execute_block.
Compares processed header fields (gas used, bloom, receipts root, BAL hash, state root, blob gas, requests hash) against the suggested header — the post-execution checks of execute_block.
Invokes post-execution validation and throws InvalidBlockException on mismatch; part of the validate-roots step.
Computes blob gas used, receipts root, bloom, withdrawals, requests, state root and BAL hash for the header — the root computation portion of execute_block.
Checks hash of the side-channel supplied BAL against header pre-execution, not the computed BAL hash comparison.
Finalizes generated BAL and computes its hash into header (hash_block_access_list step), with verify-mode comparisons.
Clones header for processing; setup plumbing.
Validates supplied BAL body (hash/size/index bounds) pre-execution; not part of execute_block logic.
Pre-execution block checks: RLP size limit, header validation, ommers, tx root, withdrawals root — the leading checks of execute_block.
Wrapper around header validator (validate_header), a separate spec function merely called by execute_block.
Enforces uncle count limit (0 post-merge), implementing the block.ommers != () check.
BAL manager/parallel-execution setup infrastructure.
Implements the MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (EIP-7934) check inlined in execute_block.
Parallel/sequential tx processor setup for BAL; infrastructure.
Checks withdrawals root matches header, one of execute_block's root comparisons.
Computes state root (compute_state_root), a separate function called by execute_block.
Computes receipts trie root, a helper (root()) called by execute_block.
Transactions root computed and compared against header, an inline check of execute_block.
Works out one receipt's bloom from its logs, the spec's bloom=logs_bloom(logs) step. It does not build or encode the receipt.
Joins the logs of a frame transaction's sub-receipts into one list. This is frame-transaction (EIP-8141) handling, not part of building the Amsterdam receipt.
Copy constructor that duplicates an existing receipt's fields. It does not build a receipt from execution results.
Compares the processed block's header (bloom, receipts root and other fields) with the suggested block. It checks receipts after they exist and does not create them.
Interface declaration only, with no logic. It reports frame-transaction receipts.
Adds log addresses and topics into a block-level bloom. That belongs with logs_bloom and block bloom accumulation, not with building the receipt.
Computes the bloom for every receipt in the block, sequentially or in parallel. In Nethermind this fills the receipt's bloom field, which the spec sets inside make_receipt.

Decides success or failure from the status code, gathers the logs and the pre-EIP-658 state root, then hands them to the receipt tracer (MarkAsSuccess/MarkAsFailed), which builds the receipt. This is the source of the spec's succeeded and logs fields. Bloom and encoding happen elsewhere.
Only forwards to the post-execution ExecutionRequests processor and adds no logic of its own.
One-line pass-through to executionRequestsProcessor.ProcessExecutionRequests.
One-line pass-through to the BAL manager.
Decodes flat requests back into lists and checks their order, the reverse of building them.
Builds the requests list in ascending type order with the type byte in front and empty types left out, matching how the spec appends. Does not make the system calls or parse deposits.
Works out the block access list item reserve for the request queues and does not produce requests.
Works out the post-execution read allowance for non-canonical predeploys.
Lists system contract addresses for the spec config.

Only does the flat encoding step (type byte + joined request data), which the spec does inline for each request type. It does no deposit parsing, no system calls to the withdrawal, consolidation or builder contracts, and no empty-output check.
Entry point for running a system transaction: runs the pre-transaction hook, sets the commit options and hands off to the base pipeline. It is part of the system transaction path.

Builds a SystemCall with the system gas limit, the SystemUser sender, the target and the data, then executes it. This matches the spec's transaction environment setup, but only for the blockhash call.
Only decides whether to hide system-account reads. It does not process the transaction.
Empty virtual hook.
No-op fee payment. The spec function has no fee step to match.
Factory that creates the processor.
For a SystemCall, uses system intrinsic gas: zero intrinsic gas plus the state-gas reservoir, which mirrors the spec's state_gas_reservoir.
Pool accessor.
Sets intrinsic gas to 0 and the state reservoir to the system-call constant, which is the spec's StateGasCosts.STORAGE_SET * SYSTEM_MAX_SSTORES_PER_CALL.
Splits the system gas limit into execution gas and the state reservoir, like the spec's execution_gas_grant and state_gas_reservoir.
No-op gas purchase.
Sends a SystemCall to the system available-gas calculation, which sets up the gas budget.
Rents a processor from the pool and sets it up.
Generic merge of a per-index block access list. It is not specific to system transactions.
Dispatcher that routes system transactions to the system processor.
General transaction execution pipeline, shared with ordinary transactions.
Wrapper around the access-list merge.
General EVM transaction execution, closer to process_top_level than to this function.
Sets up the processor and world state.

Only decides whether to pass the value transfer to the base processor. It does not build the system tx environment (system origin, value 0, SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS, state gas reservoir), run the call or record changes for the block access list.

Top-level block import: prepares the branch from the parent state, executes it via ProcessBranch and then updates the main chain (the counterpart of chain.blocks.append). It also has extra fork-choice and branch handling.

Opens world state at the parent, sets up per-block spec and blockhash context and runs ProcessOne for each block. Covers the execute-and-commit part of state_transition but not adding the block to the chain.
Wrapper that calls the branch processor and deletes invalid blocks. It only calls the logic.
DAO fork transition declaration, not part of the Amsterdam state_transition.
EIP-8253 fork-block nonce transition, a pre-execution detail of block execution.
DAO balance transfer, a historical irregular state change.
Empty DAO transition stub.
DAO fork transition check and transfer, not state_transition.
Commits the state tree. That belongs to the apply_changes_to_state counterpart, not state_transition itself.
Executes and validates a single block, which corresponds to execute_block and the validation it calls.
Block execution body (system calls and transactions), which belongs to execute_block.
Block finalization (receipts, withdrawals, requests, state root), which belongs to execute_block.
State commit helper.
State commit helper that also commits storage roots.

Main implementation of the CALL opcode, written generically for all call types. It pops the stack, rejects value transfers in a static context and charges value, memory, access and delegation gas. It then works out the new-account charge and creates the child frame.
Decides whether a new account must be charged: there is a value transfer and the target is dead. This mirrors the spec's new_account_charged check.
Only reports gas errors to the tracer.
Handles finishing a CREATE, not CALL.
Charges and stores deployed code at the end of a CREATE.
Refunds the new-account state gas after a failed child call. That is the reverse of the charge and belongs to generic_call.
Checks the sender's balance against the value, as the spec does for insufficient_balance in call.
Wrapper that reserves child gas with the 63/64 rule. This matches calculate_message_call_gas, a separate spec function.
General warm/cold account access gas helper shared by many opcodes.
Looks up code and resolves delegation. Only a building block.
Looks up code for a delegation target.
General state-gas charging, the counterpart of charge_state_gas.
General warm/cold access gas logic.
General memory expansion gas.
Applies the 63/64 rule to child gas, matching calculate_message_call_gas.
Builds the child frame and moves the value. This matches generic_call.
Charges CALL_VALUE gas for a value transfer, the transfer_gas_cost part of call.
Charges the value-transfer gas under EIP-2780/8038, the transfer_gas_cost part of call.
General new-account gas charge helper, the counterpart of charge_state_gas.
Hands the parent's state-gas reservoir to the child, matching drain_state_gas_reservoir.
Stack pop helper.

Shared CREATE/CREATE2/TCREATE opcode handler. It does the static check, the stack pops, the init-code size limit, create gas plus memory gas, the nonce-based address and the rest of the create flow (code shown is cut off after the address warm-up).
Hashing cost for CREATE2 only. It returns 0 for CREATE, so it plays no part in this spec function.
Address derivation for TCREATE (EIP-8360). Not the CREATE address computation.
Default interface method that passes the create gas charge (base cost plus init-code words) to another overload. It covers part of the spec's charge_gas step.
Charges the create base cost plus the EIP-3860 init-code word cost. This is the spec's CREATE_ACCESS + init_code_cost charge, without memory gas.
Picks the base create gas constant (CreateAccess under EIP-8038), i.e. the GasCosts.CREATE_ACCESS part of the charge.
CREATE2 salted address derivation. Not the nonce-based compute_contract_address used by CREATE.
Spec-flag dispatch for the create gas charge that InstructionCreate calls. It covers part of the gas charging step.
General memory load helper (used for loading the init code). Not the create logic itself.
